title: Mathematics: Teacher Preparation

sourceText.admission:
Admission Requirements

The Department of Mathematics has two admission pathways: Early Entrance and Standard Entry. For either pathway, visit the Department website for instructions to declare the major.

• Early Entrance: 

• Minimum course requirements: MATH 200 (or MATH 300), MATH 208

• Grade requirements: Minimum 3.8 grade for each course required for admission

• Standard Entry: 

• Minimum course requirements: MATH 124, MATH 125, MATH 126, MATH 200 (or MATH 300), MATH 208

• Grade requirements: Minimum 2.0 grade for each course required for admission; minimum 3.20 cumulative GPA in courses required for admission

The Department of Mathematics does not accept post-baccalaureate applicants.

sections.credentialOverview:
Credential Overview

The Teacher Preparation option prepares students for teaching careers in secondary or middle schools. The majority of these majors go on to finish a Master in Teaching.

This degree requires students to complete specific coursework designed to give them an in-depth experience in mathematics. Beyond learning the content of mathematics, the coursework teaches students how to communicate mathematics (and their love for the subject) to others.
sections.credentialCompletionRequirements:
Completion Requirements

51-61 credits

• Core (24-32 credits): 

• Complete one of the following: 

• MATH 124, MATH 125, MATH 126, MATH 207, MATH 208

• MATH 134, MATH 135, MATH 136*

• MATH 200, MATH 300

• Upper-division (27-29 credits): 

• Math in Context (4 credits): MATH 420 or alternative course approved by department

• Math Emphasis (12 credits): complete one of the following: 

• Algebra Emphasis: MATH 411, MATH 412, MATH 444

• Geometry Emphasis: MATH 411, MATH 444, MATH 445

• Probability (4 credits): MATH 394/STAT 394

• Statistics (3-5 credits): one of STAT 220, STAT 221/CSSS 221/SOC 221, STAT 290, STAT 311, STAT 390, Q SCI 381, EDPSY 490

• Electives (4 credits): one course from a list of approved courses maintained by the department

• Minimum 2.0 grade in all courses presented to satisfy the program requirements. Minimum 2.00 cumulative GPA in all mathematics courses at the University.

• Minimum 18 credits of graded mathematics courses numbered 300 or higher taken in residence through the UW

*May receive advanced placement (AP) credit for MATH 124 (after completing MATH 134) and MATH 125 (after completing MATH 135).
